main_text.l: INTRODUCTIO
AD lectionem LINGUÆ ÆTHIOPICÆ.
SECT. I.
Characteres quibus hodiè utuntur Æthio-
pes, quique ipsis proprii sunt ex Potkenii
Psalterio, maximè verò ex Wemmeri Insti-tu-
tionibus Grammat. Æthiop. descripta Tabula
sequens exhibet.
Scribunt verò Æthiopes non ut reliqui O-
rientales à dextra ad sinistram, sed ut nos Eu-
ropæi, incipiendo à sinistra.
Confonantes verò & vocales non à se in-
vicem separant ut Græci, Latini, reliquíque
Europæi;nec punctis vocalibus utuntur ut He-
bræi, Syri[?] Chaldæi, & Arabes, sed simul jun-
gunt, adeo ut confona cum vocali, una eadem-
que litera esse videatur, cùm tamen unaquæque
litera syllabam constituat. Unde etiam confo-
nantes 26 per vocales quas habent septem
multiplicati, figuras faciunt 182; quibus ad-
jungunt viginti alias, extra Alphabetum, syl-
labas certas constituentes, & sic in toto habent
Characteres

page.notes: The first line of the body begins with a large initial C, joined to "haracteres" as "Characteres". The word after "Syri" carries a mark that may be a j or a diacritic; read as "Syri[?]". The first letter of "sinistra" in the second paragraph looks like a long s, and was transcribed as the plain s of sinistra. The numerals 26 and 182 are copied as printed. The catchword "Characteres" is printed at the lower right, below the last line. The running title is not repeated on this page, so none is given.
